notes: The catalogue has no Raspberry Pi 3 Model B (the lookup found nothing), so a new type raspberry-pi-3 with a 40-pin header is defined. Its ports are named by function in physical pin order, so GPIO17 is pin 11 and GND.4 is pin 20.
The tutorial gives no resistor value and points to a separate calculation page. 330 ohm is assumed.

Circuit, read from the Fritzing diagram: red wire from GPIO17 (pin 11) to breadboard 1a, resistor from 1e to 5e, LED long leg (anode) in column 5 and short leg (cathode) in column 6, black wire from 6a to a GND pin (pin 20). Current runs GPIO17, resistor, LED anode, LED cathode, GND.

The breadboard port naming puts rows a-e in the 't' bank, so the diagram's rows A-E in columns 1, 5 and 6 map to 1t.a, 1t.e, 5t.e, 5t.d, 6t.d and 6t.a. Resistor end 5t.e and LED anode 5t.d share one strip.
The tutorial says the resistor can go on either LED leg, and the diagram puts it on the anode side.
The optional 3.3 V direct-test diagram (led3) is not built, because the main circuit uses GPIO17.
The photo and the jumper/solder alternatives show other ways to join the LED and resistor. The breadboard version from the Fritzing diagram is built.
